summary.gist: Iran's re-closure of the Strait of Hormuz and the US Navy's seizure of an Iranian cargo ship have shattered the fragile ceasefire optimism, sending Brent crude up 5.6% to $95.42 and dragging futures lower across the board. The dominant force today is energy supply shock — with zero tankers transiting Hormuz on Sunday and the ceasefire expiring Wednesday, the market is pricing in sustained $90+ oil and its knock-on inflationary effects. The only thing keeping this from a full rout is the AI semiconductor supercycle: TSMC's 58% profit surge and AMD's historic 13-day rally remind the market that structural demand for compute is real and accelerating.

executive_summary: US equity futures opened lower Monday — S&P 500 -0.59%, Dow -0.70%, Nasdaq -0.58% — as Iran's re-closure of the Strait of Hormuz and the US Navy's seizure of an Iranian cargo ship shattered weekend ceasefire hopes. Brent crude surged 5.6% to $95.42, with zero tankers transiting Hormuz on Sunday. The Fed holds a closed board meeting today on discount rates amid a 3.3% YoY CPI backdrop, while the yield curve's historic un-inversion (+54bp 10-2 spread) signals a bear steepener driven by sticky inflation and energy supply shock. The counterbalance: TSMC's 58% Q1 profit surge, AMD's record 13-day winning streak, and a massive earnings week (GE, UNH, RTX, NOC, ISRG, UAL) starting Tuesday provide sector-specific bullish catalysts in tech and defense.

macro_events.title: Iran Re-Closes Strait of Hormuz; US Seizes Iranian Cargo Ship
macro_events.causal_chain: Iran tightens Hormuz control in response to US naval blockade → zero tankers transit Sunday → 25% of global seaborne oil and 20% of LNG at risk → Brent surges 5.6% to $95.42 → war-risk insurance premiums spike on VLCCs → Asian refiners forced to reroute via Cape of Good Hope (+12-14 days, +$2M/trip) → Qatar LNG-to-Europe shipments at risk → Dutch TTF gas futures spike → tanker day-rates surge (DHT, INSW, FRO benefit) → airlines face fuel cost pressure (DAL, UAL margins compress) → headline CPI faces upward revision risk → Fed rate-cut expectations pushed to zero → USD strengthens on safe-haven flows
macro_events.geographic_dimension: Global — Persian Gulf, Indian Ocean shipping lanes, European energy security, Asian refinery supply chains
macro_events.historical_analog: Sep 2019 Abqaiq attack — Brent surged +15% in 24 hours; tanker stocks rallied 20-35% in one week. Current situation is more sustained given active military blockade vs. one-off drone attack.
macro_events.counterargument: VP Vance heading to Pakistan for Iran talks; a breakthrough deal could cause a sharp oil reversal. Iran has historically used Hormuz closures as negotiating leverage rather than permanent policy.

macro_events.geographic_dimension: Taiwan-centered supply chain, US hyperscaler demand, geopolitical overlay with China/Taiwan tensions
macro_events.historical_analog: TSMC's Jan 2024 guidance raise triggered a 40% semiconductor rally over the following quarter. Current setup is similar but with even stronger demand signals.
macro_events.counterargument: AMD RSI at 79 after 13 consecutive up-days is extremely overbought; AVGO RSI at 79 as well. A mean-reversion pullback of 10-15% is statistically overdue. Capacity constraints could also mean revenue upside is limited by physics, not demand.

macro_events.title: March CPI Surges 0.9% MoM on Energy Shock — YoY Hits 3.3%
macro_events.causal_chain: Gasoline prices surged 21.2% in March (driven by Hormuz disruption) → accounted for 75% of monthly CPI increase → headline CPI 0.9% MoM (vs 0.3% Feb) → YoY inflation re-accelerates to 3.3% → Fed's 2% target looks increasingly distant → market prices out all 2026 rate cuts → 10Y yield holds above 4.3% → bear steepener deepens (10-2 spread now +54bp after 27-month inversion) → mortgage rates stay elevated → housing market under pressure (DHI earnings tomorrow key read) → consumer sentiment already at record lows → discretionary spending weakens
macro_events.geographic_dimension: US domestic, with global energy price transmission
macro_events.historical_analog: 1990 Gulf War oil shock — CPI spiked similarly on energy, Fed held rates steady, economy entered brief recession. Current situation has additional complication of already-elevated inflation baseline.
macro_events.counterargument: Core CPI (ex-food-energy) remains more subdued; shelter inflation moderating at 0.3%. If Hormuz reopens via diplomatic deal, energy component reverses rapidly. The Fed's closed board meeting today may signal awareness of financial stress without requiring policy action.

affected_tickers.reason: Long-duration bonds suffer as inflation expectations rise and rate cuts are priced out
Homebuilder facing double squeeze — elevated mortgage rates + consumer confidence collapse

Broad index pressured by inflation re-acceleration removing the rate-cut put

macro_events.title: Fed Closed Board Meeting on Discount Rates
macro_events.causal_chain: Fed Board meets at 11:30 AM to review advance and discount rates → routine quarterly review but timing notable given hot CPI and Hormuz crisis → any change in discount rate signals stance shift → market currently prices zero cuts for 2026 → a hawkish signal would further flatten the front end → a dovish signal (unlikely given 3.3% CPI) would be a major surprise rally catalyst
macro_events.historical_analog: Closed board meetings rarely produce surprises, but the March 2020 emergency meeting preceded the 150bp emergency cut. Context matters more than the meeting itself.
macro_events.counterargument: This is a routine review — the odds of any actual discount rate change are extremely low. Market should not overreact to the headline.

affected_tickers.reason: Sensitive to any dovish/hawkish signal from the meeting
Broad market whipsaws on Fed headlines in current environment
